campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered renewing an interim ordinance related to state Senate Bill implementation, along with two separate hearings on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar and for Hayes Smoke Shop. The council also considered authorizing a grant application for public works funding and approving new consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Renewal of an interim ordinance implementing a state Senate Bill
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Authorization to submit a grant application through the Public Works Department
Approval of consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — May 20, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered a resolution declaring the City's intent to identify certain designated properties, as part of a formal process that will lead to a public hearing. A public hearing was set for June 17, 2026, where residents can raise protests before the Council considers final approval of the matter.
keyTopics: Resolution declaring intent to identify designated properties
Procedural steps required before final Council action
Public hearing scheduled for June 17, 2026
Process for residents to file protests
Timeline toward final approval of the designation

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 4, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine administrative and contract items, including approving minutes from prior meetings and considering several amendments to existing town service agreements. The council also looked at a plan to purchase library books and materials, an amendment to the town's legal services contract, and the monthly financial and investment report.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the June 16 and June 23, 2026 council meetings
A fourth amendment to the town's tree care services agreement with Brightview Tree Care
A fifth amendment to the town's legal services contract
Authorization to purchase library books and materials from Ingram for the upcoming fiscal year
Review of the town's monthly financial and investment report

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — August 12, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole met to finalize the City Council's August 18, 2026 agenda and review the draft agenda for August 25, 2026, deciding whether any items needed to be added or given a scheduled 'time certain' slot. The committee also considered whether any agenda items or documents required a waiver of the standard public notice requirements, set a release date for an upcoming Study Session, and received the City Manager's monthly report of activities.
keyTopics: Finalizing the August 18, 2026 City Council agenda
Reviewing the draft August 25, 2026 agenda
Adding new items and assigning 'time certain' scheduling to agenda items
Considering waivers of notice requirements for certain agenda items or documents
Setting the release date for an upcoming Study Session and reviewing the City Manager's monthly activity report

mountain-view.title: Mountain View City Council — June 23, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View City Council met to discuss the city's finances and infrastructure, including next year's budget appropriations limit, financial policy updates, and a long-term water management plan. The Council also considered several public works projects, including the Public Safety Building, Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving, and the South Bay Salt Pond Restoration, plus a closed-door session on potential litigation. Several proclamations were also on the agenda, honoring Immigrant Heritage Month, the Kiwanis Club's centennial, and City Attorney Jennifer Logue's appointment to the judiciary.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation (two potential cases)
Proclamation honoring City Attorney Jennifer Logue's appointment to the judiciary
Fiscal Year 2026-27 appropriations limit and Capital Improvement Program
5-Year update to the Urban Water Management Plan and Water Shortage Contingency Plan
Public Safety Building project and Shoreline Golf Links parking lot repaving

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — July 28, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: On July 28, 2026, the Sunnyvale City Council met first in a closed session, which is not open to the public, followed by a special study session open to the public. The main topic of the public session was an update on the city's artificial turf policy.
keyTopics: Closed session (confidential Council discussion)
Artificial turf policy study update
Special study session format for public discussion

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino Teen Commission met to discuss plans for a Bike Fest event and reviewed the Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program. Commissioners also heard about a youth-led organization called Next Vision AI, approved minutes from their June 10 meeting, and gave residents a chance to raise other concerns during public comment.
keyTopics: Planning for an upcoming Bike Fest event
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program for young drivers
Presentation on youth-led group Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes
Open public comment period for non-agenda items

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara Station Area Task Force — July 16, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara Station Area Task Force met on July 16, 2026, with the agenda largely covering standard procedural disclosures rather than new substantive proposals. The main content included legal notices about deadlines for challenging any official decisions made at the meeting, rather than details on specific station area development plans.
keyTopics: Legal disclosure on the 90-day deadline to file lawsuits challenging quasi-adjudicative decisions
Reference to Section 1094.6 of the Code of Civil Procedure governing legal challenge timelines
Procedural notices standard to Station Area Task Force meetings

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 3, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a resolution to place a Business Tax Modernization Measure on the ballot, which would shift the city's business tax structure toward a gross receipts model. Supporters of the proposal argued it would tie taxes more closely to actual business revenue, protect small businesses (most of which have modest gross receipts), and keep Milpitas competitive with other cities while simplifying tax administration.
keyTopics: Resolution to submit a business tax measure to voters
Shift from current business tax structure to a tiered gross receipts tax
Protections for small businesses with lower annual gross receipts
Comparing Milpitas's business tax revenue to other regional cities
Simplifying tax administration and adapting to modern business types like technology firms

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto City Council — June 29, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto City Council held a public hearing on a proposal for 2468 South Court, where the owners want to tear down an existing one-story house and detached garage and build a new two-story, 2,481-square-foot single-family home with a 1,512-square-foot basement. The project also shows a small attached accessory unit (JADU) for reference, though that piece doesn't need Council approval and will be reviewed separately through standard building permits. The Council considered whether to uphold city staff's tentative approval of the project's design and site plan.
keyTopics: Proposal to demolish an existing house and garage at 2468 South Court
Plans for a new two-story single-family home with a basement
Review of an attached junior accessory dwelling unit (JADU) shown for reference only
Whether the project qualifies for a standard environmental review exemption
Compliance with R-1 single-family zoning rules
